comparacio: A sharp rise of 0.071 points from Wednesday's 3.222%. November's provisional average stands at 3.266%, above October's 3.239% and a full point higher than a year ago (2.217% in November 2025).
que_vol_dir: It's the benchmark for most variable-rate mortgages in Spain. If yours is reset in December using the November average, on a €167,000 mortgage over 25 years at Euribor + 0.75%, the monthly payment would go from about €789 to about €883: roughly €94 more.
hi_guanya: Savers: deposits and interest-bearing accounts tend to pay more.
hi_perd: People with a variable-rate mortgage that's due for a reset.
per_a_leconomia: It makes borrowing more expensive for households and businesses: fewer mortgages and investment loans are taken out, which cools home buying and construction.

comparacio: Flash estimate for October, the same as in September. Core inflation, which leaves out energy and fresh food, is 3.1%.
que_vol_dir: Something that cost €100 a year ago now costs €104.90 on average. Money sitting idle loses that much buying power every year.
hi_guanya: People with fixed-rate debts: in real terms, what they owe is worth less.
hi_perd: People with savings that earn no interest and people whose pay doesn't keep up.
per_a_leconomia: With high inflation, wages and business costs tend to rise and the ECB comes under pressure to raise interest rates, which slows activity. Companies that can't pass costs on to their prices see their margins shrink.

comparacio: 60% more expensive than yesterday (€116.16/MWh). The cheapest hours are 12:00 to 14:00 (€119.33/MWh); the most expensive is 18:00 to 19:00 (€296.00/MWh).
que_vol_dir: This is the price of energy before network charges and taxes. On Spain's regulated tariff (PVPC), a kWh costs €0.131 today from 14:00 to 15:00 and €0.405 from 18:00 to 19:00: a 2 kWh wash costs about 26 cents in the early afternoon and about 81 cents in the early evening.
hi_guanya: Anyone who can shift their usage to midday, when there's more solar power.
hi_perd: People on the regulated tariff who use most of their power between 18:00 and 19:00.
per_a_leconomia: Expensive electricity is a direct cost for industry (metals, chemicals, food): it makes factories less competitive and ends up pushing up the price of many products.

comparacio: According to the EU Weekly Oil Bulletin, petrol and diesel prices are unchanged from the previous week. They remain below the EU average (€1.877 and €2.097 per litre). The figure is higher than last week's on this card because daily data from Spain's Ministry for the Ecological Transition (MITECO) was used then.
que_vol_dir: Filling a 50-litre tank with petrol costs about €86.50; with diesel, about €94.90. Compared with the average European driver, a tank of petrol works out about €7 cheaper.
hi_guanya: People who use their car every day.
hi_perd: The public purse, which collects less in fuel tax.
font: Noticias Trabajo (Butlletí Petrolier de la UE)
per_a_leconomia: Freight transport runs on diesel: when it gets cheaper, so does moving goods by lorry. The tax cut, however, means less public revenue.

comparacio: Unchanged since the 29 October meeting. In a Reuters poll on 12 November, economists expect a rise to 2.75% on 17 December, which would be the last of the cycle; markets put the odds at around 80%.
que_vol_dir: It's the official price of money in the eurozone. If it rises to 2.75%, loans get more expensive: on a €150,000 variable-rate mortgage over 25 years (Euribor + 0.75%), an extra quarter point means about €21 more a month once the reset comes.
hi_guanya: Savers, if the ECB does go ahead with the rise.
hi_perd: Anyone who needs to borrow: households with loans and businesses.
per_a_leconomia: Interest rates are the economy's brake and accelerator: keeping them high curbs inflation, but also business investment and job creation.

comparacio: Interest rate at the November auction, slightly above October's 3.026% and the highest since July 2024. Bids totalled €6,846 million and €4,045 million was sold.
que_vol_dir: Lend the Spanish state €1,000 for a year and you get about €31 back before tax. But with inflation at 4.9%, you still lose buying power: it's a way to lose less, not to come out ahead.
hi_guanya: Cautious savers who want a safe short-term return.
hi_perd: The state, which pays more to borrow.
per_a_leconomia: If the state pays more to borrow, it has less money left for other spending. And because government debt is the benchmark for many loans, borrowing also gets more expensive for businesses.
